payload.claim: For a stacked task, `worktree.prepare_worktree` checks out `spec.stacked_on` (the parent's own unmerged branch head, ahead of `base_sha`), but the exported patch — the task's sole durable product, per the docstring at line 483 — is still computed as `worktree.export_patch(container, spec.base_sha)`, so it captures the parent's entire diff plus the child's own, not the child's diff alone. `saffron/phases/package.py` (forbidden to this spec, and unaware of stacking) applies this combined patch onto a fresh checkout of the *current* remote default branch to build the child's PR (package.py:554-567); once the parent's own PR merges separately, a later re-verification (`needs_reverification`/`reverify`, package.py:625-637) re-fetches a default branch that already contains the parent's changes and tries to `apply_patch` the same hunks again, which either double-lands the parent's diff into the child's PR or fails with a false `conflicts with {default}` MERGE_FAILED that has nothing to do with the child's own work.
